title: Luca Guadagnino launches satire about Sam Altman and OpenAI with Andrew Garfield
seoTitle: Film on OpenAI and Sam Altman premieres at festival
subtitle: Feature film directed by Luca Guadagnino reimagines the company's journey as a camp comedy at the New York Film Festival.
excerpt: Luca Guadagnino's work portrays OpenAI and Sam Altman with Andrew Garfield in the cast at the New York Film Festival.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The feature film Artificial, directed by Luca Guadagnino, presents the origin story of OpenAI and Sam Altman in a camp‑comedy format. The work, starring actor Andrew Garfield, screened at the New York Film Festival and was described as a confusing technological satire.

Premiere and simultaneous editorial coverage

On the same day Luca Guadagnino's film about Sam Altman and OpenAI premiered, the outlet Vanity Fair ran a cover story focused on Altman. The journalistic piece was accompanied by portraits taken by photographer Annie Leibovitz.

The satirical approach in cinematic productions

Projects that adopt parody or satire aim to reconstruct corporate environments and institutional trajectories through stylistic exaggeration and humor. The camp genre often subverts real events with deliberately caricatured performances and narratives, contrasting traditional documentary viewpoints with free‑form dramatic readings.

Film festivals frequently serve as a platform for launching productions that experiment with narrative approaches to contemporary sectors, pitting critical perspectives against comedic representations of organizations and prominent figures of today’s landscape.

With information from The Guardian.
